name: SEC EDGAR (submissions, XBRL frames and full-text search)
description: Every disclosure filed with the SEC since 1993-1994, plus a set of keyless JSON endpoints over the structured parts of it. submissions/CIK##########.json gives a company's whole filing history; api/xbrl/companyfacts gives every number that company has ever tagged in XBRL, with the filing and fiscal period each came from; api/xbrl/frames inverts it -- one concept for one period across every filer at once. No key, no registration, no quota, and it is the authoritative copy rather than a vendor's cleaning of it.
geography: US (any issuer that files with the SEC, including foreign private issuers)

temporal.start: 1993-1994 for full-text filings; XBRL facts from about 2009
temporal.updated: filings appear within minutes; the bulk zips are rebuilt nightly

license.name: US government work, public domain
license.redistribution: unrestricted; the SEC asks only that you identify your traffic

access.auth_note: No key. The SEC instead requires a declared User-Agent carrying a real contact -- and rejects some perfectly honest ones. Read the first gotcha before you write anything.
access.size_hint: one companyfacts document is 1-20 MB for a large filer; the companyfacts bulk zip is about 1.5 GB
access.rate_limit: 10 requests per second, published and enforced; exceeding it blocks the IP for a window rather than answering 429
access.etiquette: stay under 10 req/s, send a contact in the User-Agent, and pull the nightly bulk zip instead of iterating companies one by one

probes.note: The User-Agent is overridden on purpose: the catalogue's normal prober UA contains a github.com URL and the SEC 403s it. See the first gotcha.

probes.description: One XBRL concept for one filer, every period it was reported
The same request with a library's default User-Agent
probes.known_broken: 403 on 2026-09-10, with an HTML page titled 'Your Request Originates from an Undeclared Automated Tool'. curl/8.0 is refused the same way. This probe exists so the catalogue notices if the SEC ever relaxes it.

recipes.title: Ticker to CIK, then that company's XBRL facts
recipes.code:
UA='Your Name your@email.com'
curl -s -A "$UA" https://www.sec.gov/files/company_tickers.json -o tickers.json
CIK=$(python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('tickers.json')); print('%010d' % next(v['cik_str'] for v in d.values() if v['ticker']=='AAPL'))")
curl -s -A "$UA" "https://data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyfacts/CIK$CIK.json" | head -c 400

recipes.title: One concept for one quarter across every filer that reported it

gotchas.trap: The docs say to declare your traffic by putting company information in the User-Agent. A User-Agent containing a github.com URL is 403'd anyway -- including the polite, contactable form most open-source crawlers use.
gotchas.fix: Tested 2026-09-10 against data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0000320193.json: 'Acme Research acme@example.com' -> 200, 'Headwaters Catalogue headwaters@example.com' -> 200, but 'Headwaters tnril@github.com' -> 403 and 'Headwaters tnril@users.noreply.github.com' -> 403. Substituting only the domain flipped the result, so the trigger is the literal string github.com in the User-Agent, not the shape of the header. Use a name plus a non-github contact address. python-requests and curl default UAs are refused outright.

gotchas.trap: Once the SEC has seen an undeclared tool from your IP it keeps refusing for a while, so the first fix you try appears not to work and you go on changing the wrong thing.
gotchas.fix: After a 403, wait a minute before concluding a new User-Agent failed. The block is on the address, not only on the request.

gotchas.trap: The refusal is an HTML page, and some clients surface it without an obvious error.
gotchas.fix: Check the content-type, not only the status. Same class of silent failure as the Census keyless redirect -- see census-acs.

gotchas.trap: CIK must be zero-padded to ten digits in data.sec.gov paths.
gotchas.fix: data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0000320193.json works; CIK320193 does not. Format with '%010d'.

gotchas.trap: companyfacts returns every fact the filer ever tagged, including restatements and amendments, so the same fiscal period appears several times with different values.
gotchas.fix: Each entry carries accn, fy, fp, form, filed and sometimes frame. Take the latest filed per (fy, fp), or keep only entries that have a frame -- those are the ones the SEC treats as canonical for the period.

gotchas.trap: us-gaap concept names are not stable across companies. Revenue is Revenues for some filers, RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax for others, and SalesRevenueNet historically.
gotchas.fix: Do not build on one concept name. Pull companyfacts once and see which us-gaap keys that filer actually uses, or query frames for each candidate concept and union them.

fields: cik -- the SEC's company key; zero-pad to 10 in data.sec.gov paths
accessionNumber / accn -- identifies one filing; the join key between submissions and XBRL facts
frame -- present only on the value the SEC treats as canonical for that period
fy / fp -- fiscal year and period, which are not calendar year and quarter
primaryDocument -- the filename to append to the Archives path to fetch the filing itself
